chapter: Hightower: New Orleans parades and early players
title: Joining Manuel Perez's band downtown
summary: After moving into the District, he joined Perez's band, and spent days in parades and nights in the District.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Then after I got in the district, as I told you, Zoo was playing trombone in P. Ronce's band. And most of the musicians from downtown, they didn't like Creoles, they didn't like nobody, stayed uptown, because I didn't speak French, see? And Manuel Perez, that's a trumpet player? Yes, that's right. That had the Exsulsa, that was the Exsulsa? Sometime the Enruid band. Enruid, Enruid band. And he had Joe playing trumpet with him. And he was playing cornet. And Sue Zoo was his trombone player. Zoo was one trombone player, and Eddie Atkins was the other, too. You know those two good men right there, you heard Eddie Atkins was good, too, see? And they put me in the band. So that made me the third trombone player, third trumpet player in the band, then I got all of that work with that band work. And then I found myself, after I got in that band from downtown, I found myself playing in the district at night, and just taking my horn, and taking my band uniform, and going to the parade and parade all day long. And just every day, there was a parade we had. Either that or somebody did. You see, around then we... They still had those funerals. Yeah, we had to play for the courts. They still do. That's right. Any time, they do that yet?
